Question: "What do the official Node.js docs say about checking a file with fs.access before opening it?"

### Facts

2. The reason they give is a race condition: another process can change the file between the check and the use. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "Doing so introduces a race condition, since other processes may change the file's state between the two calls."
3. What they recommend instead is to use the file directly and handle the error if it isn't accessible. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "Instead, user code should open/read/write the file directly and handle the error raised if the file is not accessible."
4. The Promise API gets the same advice: checking with fsPromises.access() before fsPromises.open() is not recommended. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "Using fsPromises.access() to check for the accessibility of a file before calling fsPromises.open() is not recommended."
5. The page's own examples call "use the file directly and handle the error" the better pattern. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "the "recommended" examples are better because they use the file directly and handle the error, if any."
